marketing.bestFor: Editorial starting point for short copy from an approved brief.
marketing.example: Draft three email subject lines for an approved November service offer.
marketing.limitation: Use approved claims only; check tone, dates and offer terms.
marketing.stepUp: Try Sonnet Medium when audience, objections and brand voice need to work together.

presentations.bestFor: Editorial starting point for a short outline from settled notes.
presentations.example: Turn approved team updates into five slide titles and speaker notes.
presentations.limitation: An outline does not establish file creation or finished slide design.
presentations.stepUp: Try Sol Medium when the deck needs a persuasive story or several audiences.

analysis.bestFor: Editorial starting point for summarizing a small supplied table.
analysis.example: Summarize a checked monthly sales table by region and flag missing values.
analysis.limitation: Check totals in a spreadsheet; a summary does not verify formulas.
analysis.stepUp: Try Sol Medium when comparisons require definitions, reconciliation or several tables.

presentations.bestFor: Editorial candidate for feedback on supplied slide images.
presentations.example: Review supplied sales slides for crowded text and unclear reading order.
presentations.limitation: Visual feedback needs readable images; it does not establish editable deck output.
presentations.stepUp: Use Sol Medium for narrative gaps; use a design tool and human review for final layout.

analysis.bestFor: Editorial candidate for explaining a supplied chart.
analysis.example: Explain the visible change in a regional sales chart using its labels and supplied values.
analysis.limitation: Small labels and cropped axes can mislead; check against underlying values.
analysis.stepUp: Try Sol Medium when the chart and source table disagree; request missing data first.

marketing.bestFor: Editorial candidate for a client proposal with clear scope and inputs.
marketing.example: Draft a support proposal from approved services, exclusions and client requirements.
marketing.limitation: Have the owner verify scope and commitments; do not invent customer evidence.
marketing.stepUp: Try Sonnet High when stakeholder needs conflict after a focused revision.

presentations.bestFor: Editorial starting point for a sales deck story and speaker notes.
presentations.example: Outline eight renewal slides linking the client brief to approved service outcomes.
presentations.limitation: Story structure and design are separate; validate claims and review the rendered deck.
presentations.stepUp: Try Sonnet High when the argument still fails to address competing buyer priorities.

analysis.bestFor: Editorial starting point for structured spreadsheet summaries and comparison plans.
analysis.example: Compare supplied Q3 and Q4 sales tables after agreeing currency and refund treatment.
analysis.limitation: Verify calculations with approved tools; no workbook access or formula execution is assumed.
analysis.stepUp: Try Sol High when a checked attempt leaves inconsistent definitions or unexplained totals.

marketing.bestFor: Editorial starting point for brand copy and internal communications.
marketing.example: Draft a client launch email and staff briefing from the same approved product notes.
marketing.limitation: A reviewer must check claims, tone and which details each audience may receive.
marketing.stepUp: Try Sonnet High when a checked revision still cannot reconcile stakeholder constraints.

presentations.bestFor: Editorial alternative for audience-specific slide copy.
presentations.example: Adapt an approved sales outline into concise buyer-facing headlines and presenter notes.
presentations.limitation: Slide copy does not establish visual polish, chart accuracy or file editing.
presentations.stepUp: Try Sonnet High for unresolved narrative conflicts; review final design separately.

analysis.bestFor: Editorial alternative for explaining verified findings to a business audience.
analysis.example: Turn checked churn totals and analyst notes into a one-page leadership explanation.
analysis.limitation: Keep observed patterns separate from causal claims; verify every cited value.
analysis.stepUp: Try Sol High when findings depend on unresolved calculations or inconsistent definitions.

marketing.bestFor: Editorial hosted alternative for copy variations from an approved brief.
marketing.example: Suggest three newsletter openings using supplied positioning and approved claims.
marketing.limitation: Confirm provider approval before supplying business data; review claims and voice.
marketing.stepUp: Compare a checked draft with Sonnet Medium if the brief or tone remains unmet.

presentations.bestFor: Editorial hosted alternative for a structured presentation outline.
presentations.example: Draft a six-slide partner briefing from approved agenda items and supporting facts.
presentations.limitation: Confirm provider approval; an outline does not imply a finished presentation file.
presentations.stepUp: Try Sol Medium when the narrative needs closer alignment with buyer objections.

analysis.bestFor: Editorial hosted alternative for source-based business comparisons.
analysis.example: Compare supplied, approved product-line summaries and list unanswered questions.
analysis.limitation: Confirm provider approval and verify numbers; thinking mode is not proof of correctness.
analysis.stepUp: Try Sol High if a checked attempt leaves material contradictions.

marketing.bestFor: Editorial step-up for proposals with conflicting audience and scope constraints.
marketing.example: Reconcile approved client requirements with service exclusions in a renewal proposal.
marketing.limitation: Resolve missing facts with the owner; never invent testimonials, results or commitments.
marketing.stepUp: Return to Medium after the message and scope pass review.

presentations.bestFor: Editorial step-up for a sales narrative with competing buyer priorities.
presentations.example: Rework a renewal deck to address finance and operations objections using approved evidence.
presentations.limitation: More effort does not validate evidence or replace rendered slide and design review.
presentations.stepUp: Return to Medium once the story is agreed; use a design workflow for final slides.

analysis.bestFor: Editorial step-up for unresolved business-data discrepancies.
analysis.example: Investigate why supplied regional totals differ from the checked company total.
analysis.limitation: Needs definitions and source values; verify proposed calculations in an approved tool.
analysis.stepUp: Request missing evidence or analyst review when uncertainty remains; return to Medium once resolved.

presentations.bestFor: Editorial step-up for a data-heavy deck with unresolved evidence gaps.
presentations.example: Check whether a supplied sales deck narrative follows the verified regional results.
presentations.limitation: Narrative review does not execute workbook formulas or validate a finished slide file.
presentations.stepUp: Return to Medium once claims and source figures agree; review visual design separately.

marketing.bestFor: Editorial local deployment option for tightly specified internal copy.
marketing.example: Rewrite approved maintenance notes as a short staff announcement after local setup.
marketing.limitation: Requires a configured, approved local deployment; operating cost and quality need evaluation.
marketing.stepUp: Improve the brief first; use a stronger approved local option if checks fail.

analysis.bestFor: Editorial local deployment option for a small, clearly labeled table summary.
analysis.example: Summarize supplied office supply totals after configuring the local deployment.
analysis.limitation: Requires setup and checked calculations; local deployment does not establish accuracy.
analysis.stepUp: Use an approved local analysis workflow when joins or reconciliations are needed.

analysis.bestFor: Editorial local deployment option for comparing supplied business figures.
analysis.example: Explain differences between two checked monthly tables using supplied category definitions.
analysis.limitation: Requires configured local infrastructure; verify arithmetic and protect the local data path.
analysis.stepUp: Request an analyst review when definitions conflict; retain the local-only constraint.
